source_cards.title: Open-Amp: Synthetic Data Framework for Audio Effect Foundation Models
source_cards.finding: The released foundation model is closed-set lookup conditioned; unseen-device enrolment freezes the network but optimises a new embedding from paired target audio and selects its initial embedding by target loss, so it is supervised target-aware adaptation rather than zero-shot reference inference.

source_cards.title: GOAT: A Large Dataset of Paired Guitar Audio Recordings and Tablatures
source_cards.finding: Re-amp augmentation improved the matching amplifier-domain transcription result but did not provide a domain-uniform gain; extra augmentation improved AMP F1 slightly while reducing DI and GuitarSet F1.

source_cards.title: Towards Zero-Shot Amplifier Modeling: One-to-Many Amplifier Modeling via Tone Embedding Control
source_cards.finding: An audio-derived tone embedding enables inference without generator retraining and is therefore a true zero-shot comparator to Open-Amp enrolment, but evidence is limited to two unseen amps, objective complex-STFT loss and an author case study.
limitations: proprietary Positive Grid encoder and corpus
unsupported EQ component in case-study target

findings: run_uni_amp addresses only the 394-row training lookup table
training table represents 150 unique capture files and test table 10 unique captures/26 rows
test_devs is created but not used by training or validation datasets
validation changes input guitar but retains training device IDs
public checkpoints use embedding dimensions 4/8 at epoch 3 rather than paper dimensions 16/64/256 at epoch 8
validation targets may be generated and cached on demand
public notebook has one render loop rather than an explicit five-pass driver
alignment-quality CSV referenced by notebook is absent
random processor state is neither seeded nor manifested
test split uses literal song-name substrings
no root or per-example licence/provenance map

knowledge_cards.claim: Closed-set lookup conditioning, paired embedding enrolment and zero-shot reference conditioning are distinct capabilities.
Choosing an initial embedding by target loss is an oracle step unless the processed target exists at deployment.
A different input guitar tests content transfer but not unseen-device transfer.
A test index is not evaluation evidence if the executed inference and validation paths cannot address it.
Checkpoint hash, embedding size, epoch, split and dependencies must match before claiming paper reproduction.
Per-device and worst-case errors are required alongside a universal-renderer average.
Zero-shot reference conditioning is bounded by the encoder domain and processor components represented during training.
High-frequency and sustain failures can remain hidden behind aggregate spectral loss.
Re-amp augmentation is domain adaptation rather than guaranteed cross-domain improvement.
More timbral variants may improve matching amp-domain robustness while reducing DI or acoustic performance.
A render count without seeded per-render provenance is not a reproducible augmentation corpus.
Best-epoch token accuracy can be invalid when high-frequency wait tokens dominate predictions.
